summary: A limited number of competitive postgraduate scholarships from the University of Cape Town for international and refugee students, for study in any discipline. They are supplementary: they add to, and do not replace, the money a student must already have for the cost of study. They can be held for one year of Honours, two years of Master's and three years of doctoral study, with renewal depending on satisfactory progress.
eligibility_notes:
The scholarships are for international students and refugees who want to study at postgraduate level at UCT (Honours, Master's or doctoral), in any discipline. The applicant's country of origin does not affect the decision. Refugee applicants must provide proof of refugee status.

You must apply for full-time admission to UCT through the Admissions Office or the Faculty Office. A funding application cannot be considered unless you have applied for admission. A funding offer is not an offer of a place to study, and the reverse is also true; the two processes are separate.

The scholarships are supplementary, so you must be able to pay for your studies from other sources as well. UCT says every effort should be made to find outside funding too. UCT states there is no guarantee of funding because the budget is limited and awards are competitive, and the main scholarship page says preference is given to senior candidates.

People employed full time (more than 20 hours a week) are not eligible for UCT postgraduate funding. The funding rules in the handbook exclude some programmes from UCT-administered awards, for example the fourth year of a bachelor's degree, postgraduate diplomas and certificates, the PGCE, LLB and BArch, and other part-time or professional programmes it names.

UCT cannot extend funding for applicants who are out of their funding tenure, which means third-year Master's students and above, and fourth-year doctoral students and above.
funding_summary: The scholarships are supplementary and contribute towards the cost of attendance; they do not cover the full cost of study. The pages I read do not give an amount. They can be held for one year at Honours level, two years at Master's level and three years at doctoral level. They are renewable for the length of the course, but renewal is not automatic: it needs a progress report signed by the supervisor and depends on satisfactory academic progress. Awards are usually paid into the student's UCT fees account, and any amount above the fees owed is paid out to the student's bank account.
programmes_note: Postgraduate study only, in any discipline: Honours (one year of support), Master's (two years) and doctoral (three years). Master's by Research and doctoral applicants who already have a prospective or established supervisor must complete Section E of the application form. UCT lists its postgraduate programmes through its faculties, and you must apply separately for admission to the programme you want.

summary.detail: Support can be held for the first and second years of Master's study, renewable if progress is satisfactory. Master's by Research applicants with a prospective or established supervisor complete Section E of the form. Any discipline. A third-year Master's student is out of funding tenure.
summary.source_text: two years for a master's degree

summary.detail: Support can be held for the first, second and third years of doctoral study, renewable if progress is satisfactory. Doctoral applicants with a prospective or established supervisor complete Section E of the form. Any discipline. A fourth-year doctoral student is out of funding tenure.
summary.source_text: three years for a doctoral degree

benefits.limit_text: Supplementary contribution towards the cost of attendance; amount not stated
benefits.conditions: Honours: one year. Master's: two years. Doctoral: three years. Renewal needs a signed progress report and satisfactory progress. Combined UCT funding is capped at an annual limit per level in the handbook (Honours R190 000, Master's R254 000, doctoral R315 000); students who exceed it may have to return funds.

benefits.limit_text: Paid into the UCT fees account; does not cover the full fees
benefits.conditions: If the award is smaller than the total fees, the student owes UCT the balance. If it is larger, the remainder is paid to the student's bank account.

benefits.limit_text: Not stated as a separate item
benefits.conditions: The handbook says UCT funding is treated as an award for the student's own tuition and living costs.

benefits.limit_text: Cost of dependents; student fee debt (except in rare cases)
benefits.conditions: Handbook: UCT cannot assist with the cost of dependents, and UCT awards usually cannot be used to clear fee debt.

A referee report, emailed separately to the Postgraduate Funding Office with the subject line 'Student Name - International/Refugee scholarship referee report'.
Section E of the form, completed.
requirements.conditional_rule: Master's by Research or doctoral applicants who have a prospective or established supervisor

requirements.text: Evidence that you have applied for admission to UCT (a separate application through the Admissions Office or the Faculty Office).

application_steps.title: Apply for admission to UCT first
application_steps.detail: Apply for full-time postgraduate admission through the UCT Admissions Office or the Faculty Office. Funding committees only consider people who have applied for admission, but you do not have to wait for an admission decision before applying for funding.

application_steps.title: Complete the scholarship form by 30 August
application_steps.detail: The deadline stated on the UCT application guidance page is 30 August of the year before you study. Complete the International/Refugee form with its supporting documents and email them to the Postgraduate Funding Office. There is one call a year; late or incomplete applications are not accepted. Master's by Research and doctoral applicants with a supervisor also complete Section E.

application_steps.title: Arrange the referee report
application_steps.detail: Ask your referee to email the referee report to the Postgraduate Funding Office with the exact subject line 'Student Name - International/Refugee scholarship referee report'. Refugee applicants add proof of refugee status. Make sure you also have other money for your studies, because the scholarship is supplementary.

application_steps.title: Competitive selection by UCT
application_steps.detail: Awards are made competitively, and the main scholarship page says preference is given to senior candidates. Country of origin does not matter. The pages do not describe the scoring or the committee. UCT's general postgraduate funding page says results for UCT-sourced awards are communicated in December of the application year; that page is written for the main funding application, not specifically for this scholarship.

application_steps.title: If you are not awarded, you may appeal
application_steps.detail: Appeals are allowed only in exceptional circumstances, such as changed financial circumstances, late applications with documented reasons (for example medical reasons), deferral of an award, extension of funding tenure or a change of programme. Send a Financial Aid Appeal form with documents to the Postgraduate Funding Office. The appeal must be in writing and strongly motivated.

application_steps.title: Register at UCT and receive the award
application_steps.detail: You can only claim the award once you have been accepted and registered in the department for the programme you applied for. Most awards are paid after a claim form sent to your UCT email, into your student fees account. If your award is smaller than your fees you pay UCT the balance; if you cannot start, you can ask the Postgraduate Funding Office to defer the award.

application_steps.title: Renew each year with a progress report
application_steps.detail: Renewal is not automatic. The Postgraduate Funding Office emails instructions and a progress report that your supervisor must sign, even if your marks are good. The award can continue for up to one year of Honours, two years of Master's and three years of doctoral study if progress is satisfactory.

notes: Source pages disagree about the current call. The older main scholarship page says the call for 2026 applications would not open because of funding constraints. The newer Postgraduate Hub page and the 2027 handbook describe a deadline of 30 August of the year before study and do not mention a 2027 call being cancelled or open. Editors should confirm with UCT whether any call exists for 2027 study (the 30 August 2026 date has already passed).
The 2027 handbook says most UCT awards, and the online funding application, are for South African citizens and permanent residents; international and refugee students use their own form.
